title: PipelineProgress
description:
The live Play-Event pipeline (HAR-145 'Live Play Event N experience'): one entry per pipeline stage, in canonical order, each reporting what the real pipeline did and when. There are no timers behind it. A stage row exists only because the code that executes the stage wrote it (pipeline_stage_events); a stage that has not run has no row and is reported `waiting`, and a stage whose outcome cannot be established is `unknown`, never `completed`. A stage that stays `running` past its deadline (the process that ran it stopped) is reported `unknown` with failure_kind `transport` and the detail `no heartbeat ...`: a poller never waits forever.

Status vocabulary: `passed`, `warning` and `failed` as a judgment are EVAL VERDICTS and are rendered by the `evals` stage alone. Every other stage that ran to its end is `completed`, which says nothing about quality (a non-eval stage that errors is `failed` with a failure_kind). `evals` is `passed` only when every result passed; any `warn`, `fail` or `abstain` result makes it `warning`, and a batch of only abstains (the judge errored) is `unknown`. Read it by polling: every status change is committed the moment the stage changes (the Play request itself stays open for the whole pipeline, so the poll is a separate request). `overall` tells the client when to stop: `running` means more stages can still arrive.

Failure vocabulary: `failure_kind` says WHY a stage did not complete. `transport` (a timeout, a cancelled call, an unreachable dependency: the stage's outcome is unknown and a retry may succeed) is never an eval verdict: the judging stage `evals` reports a transport problem as `unknown`, and `evals` is `failed` only when judged results failed (`eval_result_ids` names them, `failure_kind` is null). Any other stage that is `failed` carries a `failure_kind`.

scope.description: manifest: the Play of a demo manifest (all stages). run: one AgentRun (its own stages, with the upstream stages of the Play that triggered it when the run came from one, otherwise reported `unknown`: the pipeline did not record them).

overall.description: not_started: no stage has run. running: at least one stage ran, none failed, and not every stage is done (a Play that handed the decision to a run that has not started is still `running`). failed: a stage failed, an evaluation failed, or a stage ended `unknown` after an error (the pipeline stopped; the stage says why). complete: every stage ended (completed, passed, warning or skipped) and every message the Cliff reserved was posted when its stage ended. `complete` is final: nothing reopens it, so a client stops polling. A Cliff message reserved later (the chooser, the judgment) is listed in cliff.refs.slack_refs with its own ts and never changes an ended stage.

stages.description: Every stage, in canonical order (ingest, resolve, graph, state, decide, evals, cliff). The order is presentation order: started_at and ended_at say what actually happened first.

stageStatus.description: waiting: has not run (no row). running: started, not finished. completed: a stage other than evals ran to its end and wrote its artifact (not a quality claim). passed: evals only: every judged result passed. warning: evals only: a result warned, failed (without every candidate being blocked) or abstained. failed: ran and failed (see failure_kind; for evals, only as a judgment: every candidate blocked). skipped: deliberately not run because the pipeline found nothing to do (for example a non-material event owes no decision; detail says why). unknown: the outcome cannot be established (a transport error while judging, or a stage the pipeline never recorded).

slackRef.description: A Cliff message ref. ts is null while the slot is reserved and the post is not recorded.

refs.description: The rows the stage produced. Only keys that exist are present.

attempt.description: How many times the stage was executed (a resumed Play re-runs a stage that did not finish). 0 while waiting.

eval_result_ids.description: The EvalResults of the stage where it was judged (evals; for decide, none).

detail.description: One line: the reason for a skip, a warning or a failure; a count for a pass.

seq.description: Monotonic change counter of the stored row: assigned on insert and reassigned (larger) on every update, so a poller that remembers the largest seq it saw detects any stored change. Use updated_at for when. A status the reader derives without a write (running past its deadline becomes unknown) does not move seq. Null for a waiting stage (no row).

allOf.description: A waiting stage has no times, no refs and no failure.
A running stage has started and not ended.
A transport error is an unknown or failed execution, never a verdict; the judging stage can only be unknown.
evals is failed only as a judgment: results failed, nothing errored.
Any other failed stage says why it failed.
passed and warning are eval verdicts: only the evals stage renders them.
The judging stage renders verdicts: it is never merely completed.
